Job Description And Duties

Join an amazing team focused on advancing environmental justice across California.

Seeking someone who is enthusiastic about working with people, who is motivated to support California communities that face the greatest air pollution burdens, and who has excellent writing and organizational skills. This position is focused on, but not exclusive to Northern and Central California communities and requires occasional travel.

No two days look the same in this position. One day you might be analyzing monitoring data or writing a paper; the next, you're in a community meeting listening to residents describe pollution burdens in their neighborhood; the next, you're presenting policy recommendations to the Board.

This Air Pollution Specialist position (APS) plays a key role in implementing Assembly Bill 617 and advancing CARB's statewide strategy to reduce community-scale air pollution by working at the intersection of technical, scientific, legal, and policy topics in air quality. The APS collaborates across California Air Resources Board divisions on emission-reduction strategies and outreach campaigns. They will build relationships with residents and community leaders, and work with air districts, tribal governments, industry, and statewide and local government agencies to find solutions to meet the local priorities.

This work requires someone who is comfortable navigating multiple projects at once, thrives in collaborative environments, and values building trusting relationships with people from many backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences. This work effectively operationalizes CARB's equity goals, ensuring community voices guide decision-making and technical analyses are transparently communicated clearly and respectfully. Core competencies include written and verbal communication, collaboration, technical fluency, and a good understanding of the nuances of legal, regulatory, and policy frameworks that affect communities.

This position will require the candidate to possess a driver license and to pass defensive driving training courses, enroll in the DMV Pull Notice Program, and maintain a “good” driver status. Additionally, the candidate must be willing to occasionally work in an industrial environment including exposure to air emissions, fumes, heat, and vehicle traffic, and to wear personal protective equipment.

Job Description And Duties

The Monitoring and Laboratory Division (MLD) is seeking highly qualified candidates to join the Operations and Data Support Section (ODSS) within the Air Monitoring Support Branch (AMSB). ODSS is responsible for administration and development of CARB's air quality data systems, including the Air Quality Data Management System (AQDMS), a digital datalogger (CARBLogger), and an information portal which support it's ambient air monitoring programs. ODSS also supports regulatory field operations by providing technical support of regulatory air monitoring instruments.

Under supervision of the Air Resources Supervisor (ARS 1) the APS in ODSS will administer and develop tools facilitating resource management, data management, data collection, and data validation of CARB's air quality data systems. The incumbent will coordinate with MLD staff, IT staff, and other stakeholders to unify MLD data systems. The incumbent will work with manufacturers and internal staff to evaluate and incorporate instrumentation into CARB's air quality systems by developing SOPS, procedures, and data workflows. The incumbent will provide training and technical support for field instrumentation and data systems.

Familiarity with Python, SQL, and AI development tools are highly desirable. ODSS team members collaborate closely with other branches within MLD, divisions across CARB, external stakeholders, air districts, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Incumbents may also represent CARB in joint operations, group presentations, share technical expertise, answer inquiries, prepare project protocols and project reports, and be responsible to correspond both internally and outside CARB.

jobs.title: Environmental Chemist (Corvallis, OR)
jobs.description:
Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
4+ years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.
MUST BE ABLE TO PASS an EPA background check to obtain access to US federal property.

Preferred Qualifications

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.
2-5 years of progressive experience in laboratories accredited for environmental analyses (e.g., TNI or NELAC, state programs).
Experience working at Federal facilities.
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) experience, knowledge of Promium Element LIMS is a plus.

jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Specialist – Western Canada
jobs.description:
About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

As a Senior Air Quality Specialist, you will report to the Service Lead within our Air Permitting and Compliance (Air P&C) Service Line. You will play a key technical role in a broad range of projects across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba. This hybrid or remote position can be located anywhere in Western Canada.

The compensation range for this permanent position is $90,000 to $140,000, commensurate with experience, skills, and geographic location. We are also committed to flexible work hours and schedules, team-based work, and cross-training opportunities.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

Actively participate in and promote the strong safety culture at Onterris
Provide technical expertise and leadership on regulatory permit applications
Conduct air emission calculations to support air assessments for a variety of market sectors (this includes oil and gas, midstream, mining, power generation and transmission, petrochemicals, and infrastructure)
Complete reviews of projects’ technical content and strategy
Execute dispersion modelling assessments of varying complexity for permitting and incident assessment scenarios
Execute annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions calculations, reviews, and verification support
Support and mentor junior and intermediate team members
Manage project scopes, schedules, and budgets
Ensure effective internal communication and collaboration to deliver high-quality products that meet our clients’ unique project needs
Coordinate with internal project teams across various disciplines, including engineers, environmental scientists, technicians, physicists, and chemists
Manage client communications and expectations
Prepare technical correspondence, proposals, work plans, and cost estimates
Function effectively within and contribute to the success of a collaborative team
Contribute to business development activities to search out and identify opportunities to expand the scope and breadth of services we provide our existing clients as well as contribute to the development of new clients
Proactively engage in development opportunities to support your career growth

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

10+ years of experience in regulatory compliance and permitting in Western Canada, specifically air related regulatory impact assessment and reporting dispersion modelling, permitting and compliance strategy
Degree or diploma in Engineering, Environmental Science or related field
Professional registration in good standing with a Canadian engineering licensing board, or the ability to achieve the designation is an asset
Expertise in air emissions quantification, including GHG annual reporting and Emissions Performance Standards (EPS)
Experience with AERMOD modelling software is a requirement, experience with other dispersion models such as CalPuff, MOVES, Phast, and Aloha is an asset
Successful execution of modelling assessments required to support Environmental Impact Assessments (i.e. acid deposition modelling, visibility modelling, etc.)
Demonstrated understanding of and ability to interpret current regulations, permitting and legislation in federal and provincial jurisdictions
Demonstrated experience providing technical support and strategy and delivering projects on schedule and on budget.
Ability to effectively manage projects and business development efforts of various sizes and complexity simultaneously
Demonstrated expertise in conveying complex concepts in a clear and concise manner, both verbally and written
Detail-oriented, well-organized, and able to prioritize effectively
Ability to travel with a valid class 5 or G driver’s license with no restrictions
Located in Western Canada

In keeping with our Health & Safety Policy, individuals in safety sensitive positions are subject to pre-employment, pre-access (and in some client cases, random) alcohol & drug testing as well as drivers abstract reviews.

Onterris provides support in its recruitment processes to applicants with disabilities; including accommodation that considers an applicant’s accessibility needs. Candidates requiring accommodation during the recruitment process are asked to work with Human Resources directly.

This posting reflects a current vacancy that the company is actively seeking to fill.

Please note, we are not accepting third party agency applicants at this time.

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. For more information, visit www.onterris.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We acknowledge that these experiences and perspectives help to enrich our teams and contribute to our ongoing success. We are committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in our employment for all applicants. For US residents, click here to learn more.

jobs.title: Junior Air Sensors Scientist / Environmental Monitoring Specialist
jobs.description:
ERG is a research and consulting firm that provides a wide range of support to federal, state, and commercial clients. ERG offers multidisciplinary teams with nationally recognized skills in engineering, science, economics, public health, informational technology, and communications. We hire people with the best minds and then provide them with a vibrant and flexible environment in which to develop their careers. The qualified individual must be highly motivated with the skills to prioritize, perform, and communicate effectively in a fast-paced environment. 

ERG is seeking a highly motivated Junior Air Sensors Scientist / Environmental Monitoring Specialist to support research and development activities for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Office of Research and Development. This position is an excellent opportunity for a early-career professional interested in air quality monitoring, environmental sensors, aerosol science, atmospheric research, environmental data analysis, laboratory operations, and field studies.

The successful candidate will work with multidisciplinary teams on projects involving air quality monitoring, particulate matter measurements, aerosol characterization, environmental sensor evaluations, exposure assessment, environmental sampling, and data collection. The qualified individual must be organized, detail-oriented, and able to follow established procedures while working effectively in laboratory, field, and team environments.

Job Description:

Support air quality monitoring, environmental monitoring, laboratory research, and field data collection activities

Operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot environmental sensors, air monitoring instruments, and scientific equipment

Assist with environmental sampling, field measurements, and monitoring campaigns

Support research involving aerosol measurements, particulate matter monitoring, air pollution, environmental sensors, and exposure assessment

Collect, organize, manage, and review environmental and air quality data

Perform basic data analysis using scientific, statistical, or computational methods

Assist with laboratory testing and instrument performance evaluations

Review data for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with project requirements

Support implementation of Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) activities

Prepare data summaries, figures, tables, presentations, and technical reports

Maintain accurate laboratory records, field logs, and project documentation

Follow laboratory, field, and workplace health and safety procedures

Collaborate with scientists, engineers, technicians, and project managers to support project objectives

Travel to field locations or EPA facilities as needed

Perform other environmental research- and monitoring-related duties as assigned

Qualifications and Skills:

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Atmospheric Science, Chemistry, Physics, Earth Science, Environmental Studies, Data Science, or a related scientific or engineering discipline

Zero to five years of relevant experience, including internships, cooperative education programs, undergraduate research, laboratory experience, field sampling, or environmental monitoring

Demonstrated interest in air quality monitoring, environmental monitoring, environmental sensors, aerosol science, atmospheric science, particulate matter, exposure assessment, or environmental data analysis

Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team

Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills

Ability to work on-site in laboratory, office, and field environments

Experience using R, Python, MATLAB, or Microsoft Excel for scientific or environmental data analysis is preferred

Familiarity with EPA monitoring programs, environmental measurement methods, QAPPs, or SOPs is a plus

Experience preparing technical reports, scientific summaries, presentations, tables, or figures is a plus

Ability to follow established procedures and maintain accurate technical records

Experience or coursework in two or more of the following areas is preferred:

Air quality monitoring or environmental monitoring

Air pollution measurement or air monitoring instrumentation 

Environmental sensor or sensor evaluation 

Aerosol science or aerosol measurements 

Particulate matter, including PM2.5 and PM10

Atmospheric science or environmental exposure assessment 

Scientific or environmental instrumentation 

Instrument calibration and performance testing 

Laboratory safety or environmental field studies 

Quality assurance and quality control 

Physical and Work Environment Requirements:

This is an on-site position at EPA research facilities

Field activities may account for approximately 25%–50% of work time, depending on project needs

Work may take place in laboratories, offices, outdoor field locations, and other monitoring environments

Occasional lifting of equipment or materials weighing up to 35 pounds may be required

Use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, gloves, protective footwear, and other equipment as appropriate, is required

Some travel to field sites may be required

ERG offers competitive salaries and excellent benefits, including health and dental insurance, life insurance, long-term disability, educational benefits, FSAs, a generous 401k plan, profit sharing, an EAP, 11-20 paid vacation days per year, 10 paid holidays per year, 56 hours or more of sick leave (based on the state you work in) per year (pro-rated for part-time) and more. The salary range for all positions depends on the years and type of experience. 

ERG is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable EEOC regulations. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual preference, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.  

Please be aware, the only authentic corporate domain for ERG is https://www.erg.com.  ERG may, on occasion, screen applicants via telephone or video interviews via Skype, Teams, GoToMeeting, or another type of video platform. However, any candidate extended a job offer might be asked to meet in person with an ERG employee before providing confidential personal information associated with new employment. 

If you’re a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran, you have the right to request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access ERG’s online application process as a result of your disability. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources via email at Resumes-Lex@erg.com or call (781) 674-7293. 

ERG fosters a friendly, flexible work environment. ERGers are dedicated to serving clients who are committed to making the world a better place. We promote and recognize principles of fairness and respect in the work we do, the partnerships we foster, and the culture we value both within and outside of our organization.

Who are we?

SUEZ is a world leader in smart and sustainable resource management, and our Air & Climate unit provides consulting services and develop and deploy digital solutions that address the key environmental needs of our customers.
ARIANET, the Air & Climate unit in Italy, delivers studies, develops, designs, installs and manages cutting-edge solutions related to air quality management: diagnostic, real-time monitoring, forecast and scenario studies, for a proven customer base of industries, public and para-public entities.
To provide the best environmental solutions for our customers, we are strengthening our applied modeling team which performs studies and develops and manage simulation systems in industrial and urban areas.
In this context, we are looking for an:

Air quality modeler

Your mission

You will join the ARIANET team, and you will be involved in atmospheric modelling, concerning mainly dispersion, chemical transformation and ground deposition of pollutants at regional and urban scales.
You will mainly use a simulation system including meteorological and emission models and based on FARM (Flexible Air Quality Regional Model) chemical-transport model, developed by ARIANET in collaboration with national and international research centers and with a significant user base.
You will contribute to the multiple applications of the system, typically: operational forecast of ambient air quality, yearly air quality assessments, reconstruction of past events, estimation of sources contributions, scenario studies in support of policy planning and impact assessment studies. These activities will also include drafting the relevant technical reports and presenting the results to clients, mostly public but also private.
You will progressively participate in the development of the models’ new features, documenting them.
You will also be able to actively participate in research activities carried out within European projects and to contribute to the drafting of scientific publications.

Your profile

Who are we?

SUEZ is a world leader in smart and sustainable resource management, and our Air & Climate unit provides consulting services and develop and deploy digital solutions that address the key environmental needs of our customers.

ARIANET, the Air & Climate unit in Italy, delivers studies, develops, designs, installs and manages cutting-edge solutions related to air quality management: diagnostic, real-time monitoring, forecast and scenario studies, for a proven customer base of industries, public and para-public entities.

Air quality modeler

jobs.description:
At YVR, we are boldly pursuing a greener and more resilient future and have committed to eliminating emissions from our operations, becoming net-zero by 2030. We are driven by our purpose to serve our community and the economy that supports it. The Climate and Environment department is responsible for executing YVR’s Environmental Management plan, including reducing our carbon emissions, increasing waste diversion, conserving water and protecting the ecosystem on Sea Island. We also execute YVR’s Noise Management Plan, balancing the need for safe, convenient 24-hour travel with enjoyable urban living.

Position Overview

We have a permanent, full-time opportunity for an Environmental Analyst in the Environment Department. Reporting to the Manager, Climate & Environment, the successful candidate will be a key member of a multidisciplinary team who is passionate about creating environmental change and is looking for an opportunity to work on interesting and varied environmental projects.

Key Responsibilities Include

The successful candidate will use a unique combination of analytical expertise and relationship-building skills to lead and support environmental sustainability initiatives across the airport. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Developing and implementing environmental conservation and reduction strategies that support the Airport Authority's Environmental Management Plan and Roadmap to Net Zero Emissions by 2030, including greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting, emissions reporting, and net zero initiatives aligned with recognized standards (e.g., ISO and Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)).
Performing data collection, quality assurance, analysis, and complex modelling related to energy, emissions, carbon, water, waste, and hazardous materials management, including Scope 3 emissions and lifecycle assessments (LCA), to support environmental reporting, program development, and decision-making.
Providing environmental expertise throughout the planning, design, construction, and operation of airport facilities, incorporating sustainable building and infrastructure practices (e.g., LEED and Envision) while ensuring compliance with applicable federal, provincial, and municipal environmental regulations.
Promoting environmental sustainability through employee engagement, education, and awareness initiatives that encourage sustainable behaviours, including green transportation and active commuting programs.
Collaborating with airport employees, project teams, regulators, and community representatives to integrate sustainability considerations into airport operations and strategic initiatives, advancing YVR as a leader in environmental stewardship.

Key Qualifications Include

At least four years’ experience conducting environmental studies, research and monitoring, supplemented by an undergraduate degree in natural science, environmental studies or engineering; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
A keen analytical ability and proficient computer skills, including word processing and spreadsheets.
Proven ability to develop strong working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders and demonstrated skills and experience in conducting effective presentations and training programs.
Exceptional oral and written communication skills, including demonstrated excellence in report writing.
Knowledge of federal, provincial and local environmental legislation.
Experience with energy, air quality, waste management and hazardous materials management; experience in other areas of environmental management an asset.
Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic setting with a focus on results.

Although not required, French language skills are an asset as we are committed to providing bilingual services to our visitors and passengers. This helps us meet federal language obligations while ensuring a welcoming experience. Candidates who do not speak French are still strongly encouraged to apply.

This position is open to both Vancouver Airport Authority employees and external applicants.

Previous job performance will be taken into consideration for all internal candidates that apply for this position. As part of our recruitment process, short-listed candidates may be required to participate in an assessment process.

Salary Range :
$85,156 to $111,294 per annum, based on 37.5-hour work week. This is individually tailored to reflect your unique experience, qualifications and internal equity.

Who We Are

YVR is more than just an airport. We connect our beautiful province and all it has to offer to the world. We are all leaders and trailblazers for change and innovation, so no matter the department or team you’re a part of, the work you do matters.

At YVR, we are flexible in everything we do. We will work together to find ways to deliver customer excellence that helps us all thrive.

Whatever your background and wherever you’re from, you belong at YVR. If you have any questions about accessibility or require any assistance applying, please reach out at careers@yvr.ca.

**Introduction**
----------------

The San Joaquin County Environmental Health Department is recruiting to fill one full-time Registered Environmental Health Specialist vacancy and to establish an eligible list which may be used to fill future vacancies.  
  
**\*Additional 4% increase effective July 2027**
  
  
Resumes **will not** be accepted in lieu of an application. A completed application must be postmarked or received online by the final filing deadline.  
  
**Pre-Employment Drug Screening and Background:** Potential new hires into this classification are required to successfully pass a pre-employment drug screen and a background investigation as a condition of employment. Final appointment cannot be made unless the eligible has passed the drug screen and successfully completed the background process. The County pays for the initial drug screen.  
  
***NOTE: All correspondences relating to this recruitment will be delivered via e-mail. The e-mail account used will be the one provided on your employment application during time of submittal. Please be sure to check your e-mail often for updates. If you do not have an e-mail account on file, Human Resources will send you correspondences via US Mail.***

**TYPICAL DUTIES**
------------------

* Conducts inspections and investigations to determine environmental health problems; determines needs for corrective action and provides appropriate assistance; conducts surveys and collects data.
* Enforces and obtains compliance with federal, state and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and standards in the area of environmental health.
* Inspects food handling and processing establishments, land use applications, public swimming pools and spas, substandard housing, well systems, small public water systems, on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, underground storage tank facilities, hazardous waste generator facilities, and other environmental health programs; performs emergency response services.
* Reviews and approves plans for installation of on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, well systems, underground storage tanks, public swimming pools, food establishments, small public water systems and other related environmental health installations.
* Investigates complaints of nuisances such as vector problems, waste disposal and other unsanitary conditions; gathers facts, collects samples and prescribes abatement and control measures.
* Inspects chemical and hazardous waste storage facilities and investigates hazardous material spills.
* Gathers, organizes and analyzes technical data and prepares appropriate reports utilizing computers and computer software programs; maintains specialized records; prepares correspondence.
* Interprets environmental health laws and regulations to contractors, public and private officials and the general public; makes presentations to various interest groups.
* Provides information for the preparation of billing statements, issues environmental health permits and collects fees.
* May assist in training of Environmental Health Specialists and Environmental Health Specialist Trainees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
--------------------------

**Education:** Possession of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with course work in sciences and mathematics as prescribed in Section 106600-106735, all inclusive, of the California Health and Safety Code.  
  

**Registration:** Possession of a valid certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California Department of Health Services.

  

**License:** Possession of a valid California Driver’s License.

**KNOWLEDGE**
-------------

Basic principles of biology, chemistry, microbiology and physics; principles and practices of environmental health; federal, state and local laws, regulations and standards relative to the duties; agencies, officials and resources involved in the environmental health field; principles and methods of conducting investigations and inspections, methods for resolving problems and enforcement procedures; safety practices; language mechanics; methods of data gathering, analysis and presentation, including statistical concepts; mathematics at the college algebra or calculus level; basic public relations principles.

**ABILITY**
-----------

Conduct inspections, investigations, and reporting procedures; enforce laws and develop satisfactory resolutions of problems and violations; interpret technical written information; communicate effectively with others, both orally and in writing; present information in both written and verbal formats; operate a data entry device; establish and maintain effective working relationships with a wide variety of public and private business officials and the general public; follow written and oral instructions.

**PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS**
--------------------------------

Mobility-Operation of a data entry device; repetitive motion; sitting, standing, walking for extended periods of time; driving; occasional pushing, pulling, bending, squatting, climbing; Lifting-Frequently 5 pounds or less; occasionally 5 to 30 pounds; Visual-Distinguishing between various items, including pests and health conditions; constant good overall vision and reading/close-up work; frequent color perception and use of eye/hand coordination; occasional use of depth perception and peripheral vision; Hearing/Talking-Frequent hearing of normal speech, hearing/talking on the telephone, talking in person; Emotional/Psychological-Frequent decision making, concentration, and public contact; deal with emergency situations, exposure to trauma, grief, death; heights; working with hazardous materials; Special Requirements-Some assignments may require working weekends,

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**About ADE Consulting Group**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is a leading Australian environmental consultancy providing contaminated land, resource recovery, environmental compliance, occupational hygiene, geotechnical and laboratory services nationwide. We combine expert consulting capability with our own NATA-accredited laboratories and dedicated research and development team to deliver practical, science-based solutions for clients across Australia.

Our environmental team comprises more than 50 consultants nationally, working across major infrastructure, industrial, property, waste, government and energy projects. We pride ourselves on technical excellence, collaboration and developing our people through mentoring, training and exposure to diverse and challenging projects.

**About the Role**
------------------

ADE is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our team.

This role is suited to an environmental professional with approximately **2 to 6 years of relevant experience** who can independently deliver environmental investigations, contaminated land assessments, groundwater monitoring, waste classification projects and environmental compliance programmes.

You will work closely with experienced Project Managers, Senior Consultants and Principals while continuing to develop your technical expertise, consulting capability and project management skills. The role offers exposure to projects throughout Australia across a broad range of environmental disciplines.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Plan and deliver contaminated land investigations and environmental assessments.
* Undertake soil, groundwater, surface water and waste sampling programmes.
* Develop and refine conceptual site models.
* Interpret laboratory and field data against relevant environmental criteria and guidelines.
* Prepare technical reports, risk assessments and client deliverables.
* Conduct waste classification and resource recovery assessments.
* Support environmental compliance and monitoring programmes.
* Coordinate fieldwork, drilling contractors and other subcontractors.
* Manage project budgets, schedules and project reporting on smaller projects.
* Prepare proposals, fee estimates and variation requests.
* Supervise and mentor graduate consultants and field staff.
* Build and maintain strong client relationships and identify opportunities for repeat work.

**About You**
-------------

To be successful in this role, you will have:

* A Bachelor's degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, Earth Science, Chemistry or a related discipline.
* Approximately 2-6 years of relevant environmental consulting or environmental industry experience.
* Experience undertaking environmental investigations, field sampling and technical reporting.
* Sound understanding of contaminated land assessment, groundwater monitoring, waste classification, remediation or environmental compliance.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong organisational and project management skills.
* A commitment to workplace health and safety.
* A current Australian Driver Licence.
* Willingness to undertake field work, regional travel and occasional interstate travel.

**Highly Regarded Experience**
------------------------------

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be highly regarded:

* Contaminated land assessment and remediation
* Groundwater assessment and monitoring
* Waste classification and resource recovery
* PFAS investigations
* Asbestos in soil investigations
* Acid sulfate soils
* Environmental due diligence
* Environmental compliance and auditing
* Environmental monitoring programmes

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* Competitive remuneration package with annual salary reviews.
* Flexible working arrangements.
* Genuine career progression opportunities within a national consultancy.
* Ongoing professional development and mentoring from senior technical staff.
* Support for professional memberships and industry involvement.
* Exposure to major projects throughout Australia.
* Collaboration with ADE's multidisciplinary consulting, laboratory and R&D teams.
* A supportive, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.

**Why Join ADE?**
-----------------

At ADE, you'll work alongside experienced environmental scientists, engineers, geologists and technical specialists on projects that shape how contaminated land, waste and environmental risks are managed across Australia. We invest heavily in developing our people and provide clear career pathways for consultants looking to progress into project management, technical leadership or specialist technical streams.

**How to Apply**
----------------

If you are looking to further your career with a growing national consultancy and enjoy working on technically challenging environmental projects, we encourage you to apply.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where employment decisions are based on merit, capability, qualifications and business requirements.

Applicants must have the legal right to work in Australia, or be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate Australian work rights.

The APTIM Federal Services, LLC team is seeking a Field Chemist to support an existing project team at our Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Project in San Francisco, California along with other projects in and out of the Bay area as well as California in general. * Coordinating with subcontract laboratories
* Interpretation/evaluation and verification/validation of chemical data
* Assist in the development of plans, including selection of sampling and analyses methods
* Data tracking and evaluations against project criteria
* Preparation of procedures and reports related to sample/data collection and results
* Communication of data and comparison to decision-limits to project teams, including client and/or regulator entities, ensuring conformance to applicable technical standards as well as company policies and procedures
* Participation in project planning and execution should results indicate additional action is required

* Ability to prioritize assignments and work independently with minimal guidance
* May act as a resource for colleagues with less experience
* Monitor and control costs within own work. Solve moderately complex problems; take a new perspective on existing solutions
* Manage own time to meet agreed targets
* Ability to work outside in all weather conditions and on sites where hazards are present and PPE is required
* Able to lift up to 40lbs
* Possess ability to explain difficult issues, develop and plan solutions, and work to establish consensus
* Promote teamwork; coaches and guides others.

* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Emissions Certification and Compliance Division is recruiting an Air Pollution Specialist (APS) for the Heavy-Duty In-Use Compliance (HDIUC) Section. This section is responsible for the largest heavy-duty engine recall in history. For an engineer or scientist, this is the stuff of dreams: getting out of the ordinary and making a difference in people's lives by helping to reduce in-use emissions so that we can all enjoy cleaner air. The heavy-duty on-road and off-road in-use compliance programs are essential to protect public health by helping to guarantee that the stringent engine emissions standards are met in-use and are remedied through recall or possible enforcement action.

This job requires the APS to be a project manager for the in-use engine/equipment emissions testing programs, review in-use testing data submitted by manufactureres, conduct emissions compliance and defeat device analysis, review and process recalls to correct noncompliance, and support CARB enforcement actions and rulemaking efforts. The APS will be working with various California Air Resources Board (CARB) groups, manufacturers, and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to support testing, facilitate discussions, and investigate emissions noncompliance issues.

For the CARB-run in-use compliance programs, the APS will create test plans, direct procurement of vehicles/off-road equipment (evaluating proper operation and maintenance), collaborate with various CARB sections to have vehicles instrumented, and coordinate testing. The successful candidate will perform engineering analysis of emissions test data and complex technical information, generate clear and concise technical reports, and organize/present the results.

For the manufacturer-run in-use testing programs, the APS will review and process in-use compliance test reports and coordinate with manufacturers on the completion and compliance of the testing. The APS may also travel to testing sites and manufacturer's emissions test facilities to perform laboratory audits and verify compliance. Travel is expected to be up to 10% of the time and may include overnight or multi-day trips. Depending on the activity, travel may involve flying or driving a car or truck. In some cases, work outside of normal hours may also be required. Safety footwear and safety glasses are required.

Throughout these processes, the APS will communicate and coordinate with the engine manufacturer to support testing and when necessary, develop corrective actions, review and process voluntary/influenced recalls, and track their implementation. The APS will support CARB enforcement staff with litigation or settlement actions for in-use compliance investigations when necessary. The APS will aso support CARB ruelmaking efforts related to in-use compliance requirements.

In addition, the APS may be called upon to serve as a lead staff person for work groups and technical meetings, and to engage in outreach events with industry, government organizations, and the public.

The candidate must have excellent verbal and written communication skills to engage with a variety of stakeholders, as well as create and review technical documents.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

This position may be eligible for hybrid in-office work and in-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Boards' (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in-person attendance is also required.

The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

* Standard office environment (artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.)

jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Are you looking to join an organization that is growing and dynamic? What about a high-energy, collaborative environment that rewards hard work?**

J.S. Held is a global consulting firm that combines technical, scientific, financial, and strategic expertise to advise clients seeking to realize value and mitigate risk. Our professionals serve as trusted advisors to organizations facing high stakes matters demanding urgent attention, staunch integrity, proven experience, clear-cut analysis, and an understanding of both tangible and intangible assets.

The firm provides a comprehensive suite of services, products, and data that enable clients to navigate complex, contentious, and often catastrophic situations.

 **Job Description**

J.S. Held is seeking an experienced and highly motivated **(Senior) Environmental Scientist / (Senior) Industrial Hygienist** to join our Industrial Hygiene & Built Environment practice in Los Angeles. This role is ideal for a seasoned professional with a strong background in environmental consulting, hazardous materials assessment, regulatory compliance, and client advisory services.

The successful candidate will lead and manage complex environmental investigations, provide technical expertise on hazardous materials and indoor environmental quality issues, and support project delivery for a diverse portfolio of commercial, industrial, institutional, healthcare, and insurance-related clients. In addition to conducting field assessments, this individual will play a key role in client engagement, project oversight, staff mentoring, and technical leadership.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Lead and perform complex environmental investigations, inspections, and monitoring programs related to asbestos, lead-based paint, mold, and other environmental hazards.
* Serve as a technical resource and subject matter expert for hazardous materials assessments, indoor air quality (IAQ) evaluations, and remediation projects.
* Manage field activities, including air, bulk, and surface sampling programs, ensuring compliance with project objectives and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Oversee and interpret environmental data, prepare technical reports, and provide clear recommendations to clients and project stakeholders.
* Direct remediation and abatement oversight activities, including contractor monitoring, final visual inspections, and clearance air sampling.
* Maintain compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA, EPA, and CDPH requirements, while ensuring adherence to company health and safety standards.
* Manage project schedules, budgets, and deliverables, ensuring high-quality execution and client satisfaction.
* Develop and maintain strong client relationships by providing technical guidance, regulatory interpretation, and strategic consulting support.
* Mentor and support junior staff through field training, technical review, and professional development initiatives.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across J.S. Held to support complex projects, business development activities, and practice growth initiatives.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of technical procedures, quality assurance programs, and best practices within the Industrial Hygiene & Built Environment practice.
* Maintain and calibrate field equipment and ensure proper implementation of quality control and quality assurance procedures.

  
**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Health, Environmental Engineering, Kinesiology, or a related discipline.
* **5+ years of experience** in industrial hygiene, environmental consulting, hazardous materials management, or a related field, with demonstrated progression in responsibility.
* Extensive experience conducting and managing asbestos, lead-based paint, mold, and indoor air quality investigations.
* Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA, EPA, CDPH, and applicable hazardous materials regulations.
* Experience overseeing environmental sampling programs, including air, bulk, and surface sampling, and interpreting laboratory data.
* Demonstrated experience managing projects, coordinating field teams, and delivering high-quality client deliverables on schedule and within budget.
* Strong technical writing, report preparation, and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) review experience.
* Ability to independently lead field investigations and travel to project sites throughout the Los Angeles area and surrounding regions.
* Experience serving as a client-facing consultant and providing technical recommendations to stakeholders.
* Valid Driver's License.

**Preferred**

* Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST).
* California Lead Sampling Technician Certification.
* NIOSH 582 Microscopy Course (or equivalent).
* OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER Certification.
* Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or progress toward professional certification.
* EPA AHERA Inspector and/or Management Planner accreditation.
* Experience mentoring junior staff and providing technical oversight.
* Experience supporting business development initiatives, proposal preparation, and client relationship management.
* Experience working on complex commercial, industrial, healthcare, education, or insurance-related projects.

  
**Additional Information**

**Some of the Benefits We Have Include**

J.S. Held understands all our employees are people and sometimes life needs flexibility. We work to always provide an environment that best supports and suits our team’s needs.

* Our flexible work environment allows employees to work remotely, when needed
* Flexible Time Off policy
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* 401k Match
* Commuter Benefit

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $110,000 - $165,000. Any offered salary range is based on a wide array of fact

jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

**Role description:**

Arcadis is seeking an **entry-level** Geologist/Environmental Scientist to join our team in Irvine, CA. While this position requires both field and office work, the candidate should expect to spend 50% to 75% of their time in the field.

You will have the opportunity to join a dedicated team in Irvine, CA that prioritizes mentorship and your professional growth. The team is committed to supporting your success and providing guidance as you navigate your role.

As part of our Resilience Environment team, you’ll help improve quality of life.

**Role accountabilities:**

As part of this role, you will be responsible for assisting Project Managers (PMs) and Task Managers (TMs) in planning and executing environmental site characterization, investigation, and remediation tasks.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. It is essential to conduct fieldwork with a focus on health and safety.

Your core duties will include:

* Prepare subcontracts and oversee the work of subcontractors.
* Writing and preparing technical reports, work plans, letters, and memoranda
* Office work may include task coordination, data compilation and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file reviews, proposal writing, project strategy development, schedule and budget management, and establishment of subcontracts.
* Conduct field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work. Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our Pacific Northwest and National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable. A valid driver's license is required for the role.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Hydrogeology, or closely related field (i.e., environmental science, physical science)

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Science degree in Geology or closely related field
* Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

jobs.title: Executive Associate Dean, College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Executive Associate Dean is a senior academic leader and strategic advisor to the dean and a key member of the college's executive leadership team. Bringing the perspective and judgment of an accomplished faculty member and academic administrator, the Executive Associate Dean maintains a broad, integrated view of the college's academic programs, people, operations, partnerships, resources and priorities; identifies connections, opportunities and emerging issues across those areas; and provides strategic counsel to the dean on matters affecting the college and its long-term success.

Working closely with the dean, associate and assistant deans, department heads, center directors and other college leaders, the Executive Associate Dean helps translate college priorities into coordinated action and ensures that executive decision-making is informed by academic context, institutional knowledge and the perspectives of faculty and academic leaders. The position serves as a trusted advisor and sounding board to the dean, provides leadership on complex issues that span organizational and disciplinary boundaries, and represents and acts on behalf of the dean as appropriate.

In addition to this collegewide leadership role, the Executive Associate Dean provides executive oversight of academic operations, agricultural and commercial operations, facilities and land-use planning, and other designated areas of college operations.

Department Summary

The College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences (CAFES) at Cal Poly is one of the nation’s premier colleges of agriculture and natural resources – and the fifth-largest of its kind in the U.S. With more than 4,200 undergraduates, 16 majors, five graduate programs, and 192 dedicated faculty and staff, CAFES is a powerhouse of innovation, impact and hands-on learning. Our signature Learn by Doing philosophy comes alive across 10,000 acres of cropland, pastures, orchards, vineyards, and forests, as well as in specialized teaching and research facilities. From the Animal Health Center and Equine Center to the Center for Wine and Viticulture, Ag Tech Center and Plant Sciences Complex at the San Luis Obispo campus and Marine Transportation facilities at the Solano campus, students and faculty work side by side – tackling real-world challenges and shaping the future of food, agriculture and the environment. Discover more at cafes.calpoly.edu .

Key Qualifications

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with academic, administrative, industry and community audiences.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and institutionally across academic disciplines, programs and administrative functions.
Excellent leadership and management skills, including the ability to build alignment, develop others and lead through influence as well as formal authority.
A leadership style characterized by integrity, openness, flexibility, inclusiveness, transparency and kindness.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex and sometimes competing information and perspectives and translate them into sound recommendations for executive decision-making.
Demonstrated capacity to serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, including the judgment and confidence to offer candid counsel, constructive challenge and alternative perspectives.
Ability to move effectively between strategic and operational perspectives and recognize when an operational issue has broader academic, organizational, financial or reputational implications.
Record of successfully addressing complex issues that cross organizational, disciplinary or functional boundaries.
Demonstrated use of tact and diplomacy to effectively handle a broad range of high level and sensitive interpersonal situations with diverse personalities and to respond appropriately to conflicts and problems.
Ability to work well under pressure and maintain composure.

Education And Experience

PhD or terminal degree
Credentials appropriate for a tenured appointment at the rank of full professor within the College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
At least five years of relevant higher education administrative experience with evidence of increasing responsibility. Examples include service as an associate dean, department head or chair, program director or coordinator, center director, or leader of a sufficiently complex research or academic program.
Distinguished record of academic achievement and demonstrated effectiveness in teaching, research and service
Record of successful leadership of people, programs and complex initiatives
Demonstrated experience working across academic disciplines, programs or organizational units to advance shared priorities
Demonstrated understanding of faculty roles, academic culture, shared governance and the opportunities and challenges of leadership in a complex university environment
Commitment to collegial, collaborative and constructive interactions across the college and university

Licenses, Certificates, Credentials

Possession of a valid driver’s license or the ability to obtain by date of hire

Salary And Benefits

The anticipated hiring range for this role is $210,000 - $230,000. Note that the offer is calculated based on the background and relevant years of experience of the individual selected.

Factors in determining the appropriate compensation for a role include experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. The Anticipated Hiring Range referenced in the job posting is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position. The Classification Range may be broader than what the University anticipates paying for this position, based on internal equity, budget, and collective bargaining agreements (when applicable).

Cal Poly offers a best-in-class benefits program, including health, dental and vision insurance, retirement participation in the Public Employees' Retirement System, and educational benefits for eligible employees. See our benefits website for additional information.

About Cal Poly

Known for its Learn by Doing philosophy, Cal Poly is ranked among the top 10 public universities in the nation. Each year, more than 23,000 top-tier students come to Cal Poly in San Luis Obispo and Cal Poly Maritime Academy in Solano County to put knowledge into action, taking their learning outside the classroom as they prepare for careers in engineering, agriculture, science, business, humanities, maritime and the built environment. Cal Poly’s hands-on philosophy, small class sizes and close student-faculty mentorships result in graduates ready from day one to impact their communities, California and the world. jobs.description:
Company Description

Come grow with us.

Become part of our dynamic Water business which boasts around 600 experts across Australia and New Zealand and 6000 globally. Collaborate with top-tier civil, mechanical, electrical, and process engineers to deliver a variety of captivating projects, from small initiatives to large-scale ventures, all the way from concept to completion. At AECOM, you’ll thrive in an inclusive and forward-thinking environment where your contributions are valued.

We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging - because great ideas come from diverse perspectives. AECOM is proud to be a Fortune 500 Most Admired Company
, offering Veteran Employment Support,
a recognised WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality
, Work180 Equitable Workplace Awards 2025 Winner
and an AWEI Bronze Tier LGBTQ+ Inclusive Employer
.

Job Description

Growth & Diverse Opportunities

AECOM's Water team is delivering some of the most significant water projects across Australia and New Zealand, backed by a record pipeline of work and the strength of our global network. From major flood resilience and water security programs to renewable energy, transport and critical infrastructure projects, our teams are helping shape more sustainable and resilient communities.

As we continue to grow, we're seeking talented Water Resources professionals who want to work on industry-leading projects, collaborate with experts across the globe, and build a rewarding long-term career with AECOM.

With opportunities coming up across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Newcastle, Gold Coast, Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch
, you can be based from flexible locations Australia and New Zealand offices while contributing to projects of regional, national and international significance.

Whether you're an emerging professional, an experienced technical specialist or an established leader, we offer the opportunity to work on complex, meaningful projects while enjoying the flexibility and support to shape your own career.

Qualifications

Who we're looking for

We welcome interest from professionals across the broader Water Resources sector. Whether your expertise lies in technical delivery, project leadership, modelling, planning or design, we'd love to hear from you.

As we continue to grow our teams across Australia and New Zealand, we typically build capability in the following areas:
Flood Engineering
Hydraulic Engineering & Modelling
Surface Water Modelling
Coastal & Marine Engineering
Drainage & Stormwater Engineering
Civil and Water Resources Engineers
Technical Leadership (Technical Leads, Associates & Technical Directors)
Project Management
Design Management

We are interested in hearing from professionals at all career stages, from emerging and developing professionals through to experienced specialists, project leaders and technical experts looking to contribute to some of the region's most significant water projects.

Additional Information

Why you'll love working with us

You'll be joining a team delivering some of the most complex and meaningful water projects across Australia and New Zealand, supported by global expertise, industry-leading technology and a collaborative culture, you’ll also enjoy:
A market-leading pipeline of Water Resources projects
Opportunities to work across Australia, New Zealand and globally
Collaborative, multidisciplinary teams that span design, construction, advisory, and operations phases.
Clear pathways into major projects and clients, technical leadership, project leadership or people leadership roles
Access to industry-leading digital tools and modelling capabilities, including AI driven technology
A culture that values innovation, collaboration and professional growth

In addition, you'll benefit from:
A culture of inclusion, diversity, equity and belonging - where your unique perspectives help us create better outcomes.
Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times and hybrid work options
Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave
Volunteer and representation leave

Build the career you want

At AECOM, there is no single career path.

You may be looking to deepen your technical expertise, lead major project delivery, grow into people leadership, or expand your experience across different markets and geographies. Whatever your ambition, we'll help you build a career that aligns with your strengths and aspirations.

Join our Talent Network

If you're passionate about shaping the future of water and creating lasting outcomes for communities across Australia and New Zealand, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your interest, including your preferred location and area of expertise, and we'll connect you with opportunities across our growing Water Resources team.

Join AECOM and help deliver a better world through innovative water solutions.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion – a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation and benefits programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We also provide a robust global well-being program. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.
